entries.text: Notable Changes Added New workflows can record a replay mode that preserves every successful workflow task boundary, so activations retain their original timestamps and job grouping. Existing workflows keep legacy chunking; tasks without activation jobs are handled internally without polling workflow routines. Cloud API bindings now include v0.27.0, with opt-in user group memberships, project management, project-scoped custom roles, and caller rate limits. Workflows can call typed Nexus service operations with nexus_client, execute, and start when the experimental feature is enabled, using service definitions from the nexus-rpc crate. Calls support typed results, operation handles, and cancellation; NexusOperationError::Failed retains a NexusOperationFailureError with Nexus metadata and a normalized reason, while Serialization distinguishes payload conversion errors. Experimental StorageDriverStoreContext::namespace and StorageDriverSelectContext::namespace (requires the experimental feature) hold the namespace of the client or worker performing the store. Low-level API bindings now include namespace soft-delete and restore RPCs and task queue concurrency-limit configuration. Changed The experimental S3 storage driver (temporalio-aws-s3driver) now writes payloads stored without a workflow or activity target under v0/ns/{namespace}/d/sha256/{hash}, using the namespace of the storing client or worker (null when it is unknown), instead of v0/d/sha256/{hash}. entries.text: Changelog Added Low-level Operator Service calls support namespace soft deletion, restoration, and restore progress queries. Cloud API bindings support v0.27.0, including user group memberships, projects, project-scoped custom roles, and caller rate limit operations. SDK bridges can opt in at build time to preserving workflow task boundaries during replay, for new workflows only. The mode is recorded on the first successful task completion and defaults to off. Core handles tasks with no activation jobs internally, without polling workflow routines; see Disabling chunking. Changed Workflow task completions and failures set resource_id to workflow:<workflow_id>, on every page of a paginated completion. Activity task completions, failures, cancellations, and heartbeats set it to workflow:<workflow_id>, or activity:<activity_id> for a standalone activity. Worker heartbeats set it to worker:<worker_grouping_key>, the grouping key each heartbeat already reports in its host info. Proxies can identify the workflow, activity, or worker without decoding task tokens or heartbeat contents. Fixed Nexus operations cancelled or timed out before starting retain their cancellation or timeout failure type even when the corresponding history event omits its failure. A Nexus operation cancelled with the ABANDON cancellation type that later completes, fails, or times out no longer fails workflow tasks with a nondeterminism error. entries.text: Notable Changes Added OtelCollectorOptions::histogram_aggregation selects how the OTLP exporter aggregates histograms. HistogramAggregation::Base2Exponential exports every histogram, including custom ones, as an OpenTelemetry exponential histogram, which Prometheus-compatible backends store as a native histogram. Each series carries Base2ExponentialHistogramOptions::name_suffix (_native by default) so it never shares a name with the fixed-bucket series it replaces, and histogram_bucket_overrides is rejected in this mode. Explicit buckets remain the default. Experimental envconfig extensions (requires the experimental feature). ClientOptions::load_from_config_with_extensions calls each ClientConfigExtension in order with the loaded profile and environment, and registers any client plugin it returns. Extension config lives in [profile.<name>.ext.<extension>] TOML tables, exposed raw as ClientConfigProfile::ext and never rejected by strict mode. Experimental external storage (requires the experimental feature). DataConverter::with_external_storage offloads payloads at or above a size threshold to a user-supplied StorageDriver, replacing them in history with small references that workers and clients resolve transparently. Drivers are told the workflow or standalone activity each payload is stored for, and may receive concurrent requests. entries.text: Changelog Added A local activity's ActivityTask.Start has workflow_task (field 21), with the started event id, attempt and start time of the workflow task in which Core dispatched it. workflow_task also has previous_started_event_id, previous_attempt and previous_started_time, which name the run's last completed workflow task, and failed_tasks, the started event ids of the run's last 100 failed or timed out workflow tasks. Retries that Core runs locally keep the value. Core leaves it unset for other activities. Client environment config profiles include the raw TOML tables under profile.<name>.ext, keyed by extension name, for SDK envconfig extensions. Strict mode accepts any content under ext. The C bridge's profile JSON includes them as an ext object, with TOML datetimes as strings. The C bridge's shared dev and test server options accept a startup timeout in milliseconds, with zero selecting the five-second default. The OTLP metrics exporter can export histograms as OpenTelemetry exponential histograms, which Prometheus-compatible backends store as native histograms, when an SDK enables the option, including through the C bridge. It applies to every histogram, including custom ones, and names each series with a suffix, _native by default, so it never shares a name with the fixed-bucket series it replaces. entries.text: Changelog Added WorkflowStartOptions::versioning_override and WorkflowUpdateWithStartOptions::versioning_override support pinned, auto-upgrade, and one-time deployment routing for client-started workflows, including signal-with-start and update-with-start. Pinned and auto-upgrade overrides require Temporal Server 1.28.0 or later; one-time routing requires Temporal Server 1.32.0 or later. Experimental ChildWorkflowOptions::versioning_override can pin, auto-upgrade, or one-time route a child workflow independently of its parent, using VersioningOverride. Requires Temporal Server 1.32.0 or later. Rejected overrides are reported as StartChildWorkflowExecutionFailedCause::InvalidVersioningOverride; missing child namespaces are now distinguished by StartChildWorkflowExecutionFailedCause::NamespaceNotFound. Adds experimental OpenTelemetry integration tracing client, Workflow, and Activity operations and propagating trace context across Temporal invocations. Use OpenTelemetryPlugin::builder() with the experimental and opentelemetry features to configure a SimplePlugin. Fixed temporalio-common's build script now generates its payload-visitor implementations in a stable order. The generated code was emitted in HashSet/HashMap iteration order, so its content changed on every build and a compilation cache such as sccache missed temporalio-common and every crate downstream of it on every build. Autoscaled task pollers now preserve polling concurrency after transient cancellations and time

entries.summary: Child workflow commands, including those submitted through the C bridge, support pinned,; auto-upgrade, and one-time worker deployment versioning overrides on Temporal Server 1.32.0; or later. Child-start resolutions…
entries.text: Changelog Added Child workflow commands, including those submitted through the C bridge, support pinned, auto-upgrade, and one-time worker deployment versioning overrides on Temporal Server 1.32.0 or later. Child-start resolutions distinguish invalid versioning overrides and missing namespaces from other start failures. Fixed Task-poll targets no longer decrease after cancelled or timed-out polls. Affected pollers still retain their slot during backoff, while resource-exhaustion errors still reduce the target. Replay now preserves which local activity results were delivered together for newly recorded histories. This prevents local activity scheduling which was conditional on local activity resolution order from assigning recorded results to different handles. Older markers keep their existing behavior. Workflow poll balancing now lets non-sticky pollers use capacity after sticky pollers reach their configured or autoscaled polling limit. Every path that fails a workflow task now only reports the failure to server on the task's first attempt, and later attempts are left to time out. Previously PayloadsTooLarge failures and history fetch failures were re-reported on every attempt. The workflow_task_execution_failed metric is now recorded for every failed workflow task attempt, including attempts whose failure was not sent to the server, and its failure_reason tag distinguishes GrpcMessageTooLarge, PayloadsTooLarge, and RequestTooLarge on every path.
